newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Portuguese Liberals defect to European Peoples Party.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese Liberals defect to European Peoples Party.

text.p: The eight Portuguese members of the small Liberal group in the European Parliament defected on Wednesday to the powerful Christian Democrat European People's Party.
The decision, taken last week by the Portuguese Social Democrat Party (PSD) to which they belong, is a blow to the Liberal group, which is now reduced to 43 members.
The EPP, the second largest group in Parliament after the 215-strong Socialist group, now has 182 members.
Liberal leader Gijs de Vries tried unsuccessfully to prvent the move.
In a statement issued on October 24, he said the EPP "holds views which are fundamentally at odds with the interests of Portugal.
"Many of its interests are diametrically opposed to the policies of the PSD."
"It stems from a problem in the PSD in Portugal," an official with the Liberal group told Reuters.
Now out of office in Portugal, the PSD feels that their best international forum is the EPP, which boasts five prime ministers among its senior politicians, the official said.

"It is difficult for the PSD to have a voice in Europe if it is not in a big European party," MEP Antonio Capucho, the leader of the PSD team, told Reuters recently, adding that the PSD did not have much ideological affinity with the Liberals.
In addition, issues of concern to southern European tended to be left aside in the Liberal group, which is largely composed of Belgians, Danes, Finns and Dutchmen, he said.

The EPP's new members hope to reap some reward for swelling the party's ranks, namely that Capucho will be named as one of the EPP's four parliamentary vice-presidents, according to new EPP member Carlos Costa Neves.

Elections for the 14 posts of vice-president are due to take place next January alongside the election of a new President, widely tipped to be the Spanish Conservative Jose Maria Gil- Robles Gil-Delgado.
The EPP is due to name their presidential candidate on November 13.
